title: Tell me how your team is doing and I'll tell you what to play
desc: With two games to pick from, here are the situations where each one works best.
item1_desc: Nobody knows anything about them, and asking during the welcome round feels awkward. In three rounds the team already has something to remember about the newcomer.
item2_desc: Ten minutes to unwind before closing the session. Nothing to prepare: code, deck, and play.
item3_desc: Works the same over video call: everyone writes from their phone and the rest votes at the same time.
item4_desc: Twelve people who don't know each other yet. The fastest way to learn names and give them a story.
item5_desc: The classic. Pull out the no-filter deck only if you know the table in front of you well.
item6_title: Friday afternoon and nobody's starting anything
item6_desc: A quick round before closing the laptop, with the wildest answer you can think of.
item7_title: Nobody speaks up in big meetings
item7_desc: Voting is anonymous until it's revealed. It costs a lot less to take part than to raise your hand.
